### Vocabulary

Renamed field values cannot be aliased the way paths are, so they a

re chosen
by header. Send `x-mcpjam-api-vocabulary: 2` and the renamed values read
canonically:

| Field | Vocabulary 1 | Voca

bulary 2 |
| - | - | - |
| session `sourceType` | `scenario` | `study` |
| session `parentRef.kind` | `scenario`, `journeyRun`
| `study`, `goalRun` |\n| session `parentRef` ids | `scenarioId`, `journeyRunId`, `journeyRefId` | `studyId`, `goalRunId`, `goalRe

fId` |
| share `resourceType` (field AND path segment) | `scenario` | `study` |

Absent means `1`, which is byte-for-byte today
's contract. Any other value is a\n`400`. On the way IN, a vocabulary-2 request may name a filter or a path segment\nby either spe
lling; a vocabulary-1 request may use only the legacy one. A response that varies by vocabulary sends\n`Vary: x-mcpjam-api-vocabul

ary`.

This is a **separate header** from `x-mcpjam-eval-vocabulary`, which is
eval-scoped by name and moves on its own schedul
e. A deployment may speak one\nand not the other, so read\n`GET /projects/{projectId}/capabilities` (`apiVocabulary` and `vocabula

ry` are
two blocks) before sending either. With the SDK:
`new PlatformApiClient({ …, apiVocabulary: 2 })`, or
`client.withApiVo

cabulary(2)` on one you already hold.

Permalink resource types work differently: `study` and
`goal_run` are the canonical keys
, `user_testing_scenario` and `journey_run`\nstill resolve to the same routes, and which one a response carries follows the\nOPERA
TION rather than the header; a renamed operation derives the canonical\nkey, its deprecated twin the old one. `capabilities.apiVoc

abulary.resourceTypes`
lists both.

# Local Evals

> Run an MCPJam eval suite file on your
machine with mcpjam test with local results and an MCPJam identity\n\n`mcpjam test <file>` runs an MCPJam suite file locally: it
connects your MCP servers, drives each case's prompts through a model, grades the transcript with the same assertions a hosted run
uses, and decides the run with the same verdict policy. Bring your own provider key and authenticate the run with MCPJam. With MC
PJam-hosted inference it uses your existing CLI login and billing.\n\nResults are **never uploaded**. The command writes results t
o your terminal and, if you ask, to a report file. It records the run start with MCPJam. Like every command, it sends the CLI's si
ngle anonymous [telemetry](https://docs.mcpjam.com/cli/telemetry.md) event, which `--no-telemetry` or `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` turns off;

the run adds no telemetry of its own.

## Eval identity and local data

Run `mcpjam cloud login` locally, or set `MCPJAM_API_K
EY` to an organization `sk_` key in CI. The SDK also accepts `apiKey` or `mcpjamAuth` in run options. Explicit credentials take pr
ecedence over `MCPJAM_API_KEY`, which takes precedence over the saved CLI login. An invalid explicit credential never falls back t
o another account. CI never starts an interactive login. Ask an organization admin for a key if you cannot create one.\n\nEvery lo
gical run needs an online start response. MCPJam retries transient failures within ten seconds, then stops before execution. A pri
or successful run does not enable offline execution. The CLI resolves the project using its existing `--project`, environment, and
linked-project settings; a key can only access its own organization.\n\nWith results uploads disabled, the start-run request send
s only the credential in the authorization header, any MCPJam API headers you configure through the SDK's `inference.resolveMcpjam
`, project selection, a new run-start ID, client version and surface (SDK, CLI, or Vitest), planned iteration count, provider name
s, and whether a client profile is used (`unknown` for custom executors). The server resolves the organization and account. The st
art-run request sends no prompts, outputs, tool calls, or server URLs. MCPJam-hosted inference still sends prompts through MCPJam
to the model, as before. Retries reuse the same ID. Planned iterations are intent, not completed usage or a charge. This release a
dds no debit, quota draw, or balance refusal.\n\n`DO_NOT_TRACK`, `MCPJAM_TELEMETRY_DISABLED`, and CLI telemetry settings disable a
nalytics, not the required run-start request. Results remain local unless result uploading is enabled separately.\n\n## Quick star

t

### 1. Write a suite

Save this as `.mcpjam/evals/example.yaml`:

```yaml theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
schemaVers

ion: "2"
mode: agentWorkflow
reportingMode: standard
suite:
 id: s_notes_example
 name: Notes server
target:
 servers:

- name: notes
defaults:
 judge:
 enabled: false
 model: anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5
 iterations: 1
 passThreshol

d: 1
 validity: {}
cases:
 - id: c_reads_a_note
 title: reads the note it was asked about
 steps:
 - id: s1

kind: prompt
 prompt: What does note 7 say?
 - id: a1
 kind: assert
 assertion:
 typ

e: toolCalledAtLeastOnce
 toolName: read_note
 - id: c_never_deletes
 title: never deletes when only asked to read

steps:
 - id: s1
 kind: prompt
 prompt: Summarize note 7.
 - id: a1
 kind: assert

assertion:
 type: toolNeverCalled
 toolName: delete_note
```

`mcpjam cloud eval validate --file .mcpjam

/evals/example.yaml` checks the file offline, with no account.

### 2. Configure the server

`mcpjam test` binds each `target.
servers[].name` to a local MCP config. The simplest is a `.mcp.json` next to where you run the command:\n\n```json theme={\"theme\

heme={"theme":"css-variables"}
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=[REDACTED]
mcpjam test .mcpjam/evals/example.yaml
```

### 4. Fai
l one on purpose, then rerun it\n\nChange `toolName: read_note` to `toolName: echo` in the first case and run again: the command e
xits `1` and names the failing assertion. Fix it, then rerun just that case and keep a report:\n\n```bash theme={\"theme\":\"css-v

ariables"}
mcpjam test .mcpjam/evals/example.yaml --case c_reads_a_note --reporter junit-xml --out reports/local.xml
```

`--

case` takes the exact authored id and is repeatable.

## Server bindings

For each target server name, the first source with a
n entry wins; the whole entry, never a field-level merge:\n\n1. `--server <name>=<url>` (repeatable; HTTP(S) only). For a suite wi
th exactly one target, `--url` / `--command` and their auth flags bind it instead.\n2. `--mcp-config <path>`: an explicit MCP JSON

config. A missing or invalid explicit file fails setup.
3. `./.mcp.json`
4. `./.mcpjam/mcp.json`

Paths are relative to the d
irectory you run the command in, not to the suite file. An explicit `--mcp-config` can bind some servers while the two conventiona
l files still supply the rest. A lower-precedence file is read only while names remain unbound, and entries for servers the suite
does not target are ignored; their processes are never started. Every name still unbound is reported together (exit `4`).\n\nConfi
g entries use the standard `mcpServers` shape (`command`/`args`/`env`/`cwd` for stdio, `url`/`headers` for HTTP, with `type`/`tran
sport` spellings such as `stdio`, `http`, `sse`, `streamable-http`). `${VAR}` and `${VAR:-default}` are expanded in the winning en
tries only; an unset `${VAR}` fails setup naming the variable, never its value. Nothing is shell-expanded. A relative `cwd` (or `c
redentialsFile`) resolves against the config file's directory; a stdio entry with no `cwd` runs in the invocation directory.\n\nOn

e credential is never shared across servers: servers that need their own auth each get their own config entry.

## Inference
